reading: The input is the left half of a symmetric outline. Mirror it about the vertical line just right of its rightmost column, then output only the interior of the completed outline, filled with the outline's colour (the outline itself is erased).
verb: complete by mirror and fill interior

slots.axis: vertical line just right of the object's max column
slots.output: interior cells of the mirrored-completed outline only; everything else background

why: on every pair the filled cells are exactly the cells strictly inside the outline formed by the object plus its mirror image

reading: A 5 cell has an arm of 2s attached on one side. The arm rotates 90 degrees clockwise about the 5 (same length); the old arm cells become 3.

slots.arm: the straight run of 2s touching the pivot
slots.new arm: arm rotated 90 degrees clockwise around the pivot, colour 2

why: on every pair the new 2 run has the old run's length and points in the direction 90 degrees clockwise from the old one; old run cells are 3

reading: Each grey square outline gets its hollow interior filled with a colour chosen by interior size: 1x1 -> 6, 2x2 -> 7, 3x3 -> 8.
why: every enclosed background cell is filled and the fill colour depends only on the enclosing square's interior size

reading: The 1-row input becomes a square grid (width x width). From the single 2 two diagonal 2-lines go down-left and down-right to the borders (a V). Below the left arm, parallel diagonals of 1 run down-right (parallel to the right arm), spaced 4 columns apart, i.e. on cells with x - y = apex_col - 4k (k >= 1), starting just below the left arm and running to the border.

slots.size: output is W x W, first row = input row
slots.V: 2 diagonals from apex down-left and down-right to border
slots.hatch: colour 1 down-right diagonals x - y = apex_col - 4k, k>=1, only on cells below the left arm

why: on every pair the 1 cells are exactly the cells below the left 2 arm on diagonals x - y congruent to the apex column mod 4

reading: Every full row and full column that contains no background cell (all 0 lines) is recoloured to 2.

new_rows.name: full_lines
new_rows.datalog:
row(Y) :- px(Y, X, C).
col(X) :- px(Y, X, C).
gaprow(Y) :- px(Y, X, C), !cell(Y, X, C).
gapcol(X) :- px(Y, X, C), !cell(Y, X, C).
full_lines(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), row(Y), !gaprow(Y).
full_lines(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), col(X), !gapcol(X).

why: every cell of a row or column made entirely of non-background (0) becomes 2; nothing else changes

reading: The output is a 3x3 grid of input-sized blocks; a block gets a copy of the input where the input cell has the input's most common colour, otherwise it is empty (0).
why: block (i,j) is the input exactly when input[i][j] is the most common colour, else all 0

reading: Full background-coloured columns cut the grid into vertical zones, each with one non-background colour. In each zone the background cells take the colour of the next zone to the right (the last zone takes the first zone's colour); separator columns stay.

slots.zones: column stripes cut by full columns of the background colour
slots.subject: background cells inside each zone
slots.colour: the non-background colour of the next zone to the right, cyclic

why: on both pairs zone i's background becomes zone (i+1 mod n)'s colour; non-background cells and separator columns unchanged

reading: Short runs of 1 on the grid border, aligned with a hollow square, mark directions: the square is repeated edge to edge (period = its size) from its position to that border; the 1 markers are erased (overwritten). Squares without a marker stay as they are.

slots.direction: towards a border run of 1s aligned with the square's rows or columns
slots.repeat: copies of the square placed adjacent, period = square size, until the border (clipped)

why: every row/column band between a square and its aligned border marker is filled with copies of the square; no 1 remains

reading: Some solid rectangles have a one-cell-wide tail sticking out of one side. Each such rectangle slides in the tail's direction by the tail's length, and the tail is erased; rectangles it used to overlap are shown complete.

slots.subject: each rectangle with an attached 1-wide line (tail)
slots.direction: the tail's direction away from the rectangle
slots.others: rectangles without tails stay, uncovered parts restored as full rectangles

why: every tailed rectangle keeps its shape and is shifted by exactly its tail length along the tail; tails vanish

reading: Tile the input 3x3. Then for every non-background cell, fill its entire row with 1 (except the coloured cells) and put 3 at its up-left and down-right diagonal neighbours.

slots.row: each row containing a coloured cell becomes 1 everywhere except the coloured cells
slots.diagonals: 3 at (y-1,x-1) and (y+1,x+1) of each coloured cell, within the grid

why: on every pair the output equals the 3x3 tiling with full 1 rows through coloured cells and 3 on their main-diagonal neighbours
invariants: coloured cells and their positions in the tiling
